extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers of Registered Reports submitted to the journal Learning & Instruction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria for Stage 1 (protocol/pre-registration) and Stage 2 (full manuscript) Registered Report submissions to Learning & Instruction, covering required manuscript content, methodological and analytic standards, registration and data-archiving requirements, and decision/withdrawal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports format
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and proposed analyses are pre-registered and reviewed prior to research being conducted; high quality protocols are provisionally accepted for publication before data collection commences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This format is designed to minimize publication bias and research bias in hypothesis-driven research, while allowing exploratory (unregistered) analyses and serendipitous findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 manuscript components
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 manuscripts will include only an Introduction, Methods (including proposed analyses), and Pilot Data (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial submissions should include key research question, background literature, hypotheses, experimental procedures, analysis pipeline, a statistical power analysis (or Bayesian equivalent), and pilot data where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the research question(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the importance of the research question(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors triage Stage 1 submissions for high scientific significance; authors are encouraged to refer to replication value and high-value replication studies are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic, rationale, and plausibility of hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the logic, rationale, and plausibility of the proposed hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction must provide a review of relevant literature that motivates the research question and a full description of experimental aims and hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness and feasibility of methodology and analysis plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess the soundness and feasibility of the methodology and analysis pipeline (including statistical power analysis where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include feasibility, detailed analysis pipeline, and appropriate power/Bayesian planning; proposals judged on scientific rigour and feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological detail sufficient for exact replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the clarity and degree of methodological detail is sufficient to exactly replicate the proposed experimental procedures and analysis pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods should provide a description of experimental procedures in sufficient detail to allow another researcher to repeat the methodology exactly, without requiring further information. These procedures must be adhered to exactly in subsequent experiments or Stage 2 manuscript can be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specified outcome-neutral tests and quality checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors have pre-specified sufficient outcome-neutral tests for ensuring that the results obtained are able to test the stated hypotheses, including positive controls and quality checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-neutral tests might include quality checks such as absence of floor/ceiling effects, lack of outliers, or other checks that ensure successful testing of the stated hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 editorial outcomes and In-Principle Acceptance (IPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following Stage 1 peer review manuscripts will be accepted, offered the opportunity to revise, or rejected outright. High-standard proposals will be issued an in principle acceptance (IPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPA indicates the article can be published pending successful completion of the study according to the pre-registered methods and analytic procedures, passing of all pre-specified quality checks, and a defensible and evidence-based interpretation of the results. IPA does not guarantee automatic acceptance at Stage 2; even minor deviations may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory time-stamped protocol registration after IPA
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors receive an in principle acceptance of their Stage 1 registered report, they must register the approved protocol on a recognized repository, either publicly or privately under embargo until submission of the Stage 2 manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A time-stamped, independent registration of the protocol is mandatory under journal policy; the protocol should be registered unchanged from its approved state, with the time-stamp preceding implementation of the approved study design. Recommended repositories include osf.io/rr/. Users must ensure author identities are not revealed to preserve double-blind review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 raw data and materials sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: At Stage 2 submission, authors must upload their raw data, digital study materials, and laboratory log to a publicly accessible file-sharing service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raw data must be freely available in a public repository and appropriately time stamped to show data was collected after IPA. Authors should upload relevant analysis scripts and experimental materials (e.g., stimuli & presentation code). When the original study is in another language, provide translations of materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data provenance and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must collectively certify in the resubmission Cover Letter that all nonpilot data was collected after the date of IPA and provide a basic laboratory log outlining dates of data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lab log should be uploaded to the same public archive as the data, with a link provided in the resubmission Cover Letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 assessment: data satisfy approved outcome-neutral conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers at Stage 2 will appraise whether the data are able to test the authors’ proposed hypotheses by satisfying the approved outcome-neutral conditions (such as quality checks, positive controls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to satisfy outcome-neutral conditions can lead to rejection even if procedures were followed; reviewers may request additional post hoc tests but authors are not obliged to perform them unless necessary to satisfy Stage 2 criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 assessment: fidelity to approved Introduction/hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess whether the Introduction, rationale and stated hypotheses are the same as the approved Stage 1 submission (required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apart from minor stylistic revisions, the Introduction cannot be altered from the approved Stage 1 submission. Any textual changes must be clearly marked in the Stage 2 submission. New literature appearing after IPA should be covered in the Discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 assessment: adherence to registered procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess whether the authors adhered precisely to the registered experimental procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any deviation from stated experimental procedures, regardless of perceived minor significance, could lead to rejection at Stage 2. If alterations are needed due to unforeseen circumstances authors must consult the editor prior to completion of data collection; minor changes may be permitted at editorial discretion and must be reported in Stage 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 assessment: justification and soundness of unregistered post hoc analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess whether any unregistered post hoc analyses added by the authors are justified, methodologically sound, and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unplanned exploratory analyses are admissible in a separate section of the Results titled 'Exploratory analyses'. Such analyses must be clearly justified, appropriately caveated, and authors should avoid basing conclusions entirely on statistically significant post hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 assessment: conclusions justified by data
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess whether the authors’ conclusions are justified given the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions at Stage 2 will not be based on perceived importance, novelty, or conclusiveness of the results; reviewers may note such opinions but they will not influence editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: full description of sample characteristics and inclusion/exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods must give full description of proposed sample characteristics, including criteria for data inclusion and exclusion (e.g. outlier extraction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures for objectively defining exclusion criteria due to technical errors or other reasons must be specified, including details of how and under what conditions data would be replaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods: precise reproducible procedure descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of experimental procedures in sufficient detail to allow another researcher to repeat the methodology exactly, without requiring further information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedures must be adhered to exactly in the subsequent experiments or any Stage 2 manuscript can be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis plan: pre-processing, planned analyses and contingencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed analysis plan must include all pre-processing steps and a precise description of all planned analyses, including appropriate correction for multiple comparisons; any covariates or regressors must be stated and contingencies specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where analysis decisions are contingent on the outcome of prior analyses, these contingencies must be specified and adhered to. Only pre-planned analyses can be reported in the main Results section of Stage 2 submissions; unplanned exploratory analyses should be in a separate Results section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequentist a priori power analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies involving frequentist statistical inference should include an a priori statistical power analysis; estimated effect sizes should be justified with reference to existing literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because publication bias overinflates published estimates, power analysis must be based on the lowest available or meaningful estimate of the effect size. For frequentist analysis plans, the a priori power can be 0.8 or higher for all proposed hypothesis tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bayesian analysis planning and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies involving Bayesian hypothesis testing should include appropriate sample sizes so that either a Bayes factor can be calculated, or other Bayesian estimation procedure implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient technical detail should be given (e.g., distributions of priors, number of chains, convergence criteria, and criteria for Bayesian inference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreseen quality control procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Full descriptions should be provided of foreseen quality control of data, which ensure successful testing of the stated hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality checks might include the absence of floor or ceiling effects in data distributions, lack of outliers, or other checks; these tests should be pre-specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and resubmission date
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts must include a timeline for completion of the study and proposed resubmission date if Stage 1 review is successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover letter should include an anticipated timeline for completing the study if the initial submission is accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective methods written in future tense (Stage 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any description of prospective methods or analysis plans should be written in future tense in the Stage 1 manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At Stage 2 these descriptions should be changed to past tense, and any textual changes must be clearly marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot data policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilot Data are optional and can be included to establish proof of concept, effect size estimations, or feasibility of proposed methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any pilot experiments will be published with the final version of the manuscript and will be clearly distinguished from data obtained for the pre-registered experiment(s). Other than pre-registered and approved pilot data, no data acquired prior to the date of IPA is admissible in the Stage 2 submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome of all registered analyses must be reported in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors reporting null hypothesis significance tests are required to report exact p values and effect sizes for all inferential analyses. Additional unregistered analyses are admissible but must be justified, caveated, and placed in an 'Exploratory analyses' section; authors should avoid basing conclusions entirely on post hoc analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data archiving vs supplementary material
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data itself should be archived in a public repository rather than submitted to the journal as supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary figures, tables, or text can either accompany the paper as standard supplementary information or be archived together with the data; raw data should be archived (not just submitted as supplementary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter requirements for Stage 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter should include a brief scientific case for consideration, statement confirming necessary support and approvals are in place, an anticipated timeline, and a statement confirming authors agree to share raw data, digital study materials, and laboratory log for published results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are welcome to submit pre-submission enquiries for advice on suitability, but editorial board will not send manuscripts for in-depth review until a complete Stage 1 submission has been considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deviations after IPA and editorial consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the pre-registered protocol is altered after IPA due to unforeseen circumstances (e.g. change of equipment or unanticipated technical error), authors must consult the editor in charge immediately and prior to completion of data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor changes may be permitted according to editorial discretion and reported in Stage 2; substantial alterations require withdrawal and resubmission as a new Stage 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript withdrawal and public recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors with IPA may withdraw their manuscript; withdrawals will be publicly recorded in 'Withdrawn Registrations' with authors, proposed title, abstract from approved Stage 1 submission, and brief reason(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial withdrawals are not possible (entire paper must be withdrawn). Studies not completed by agreed Stage 2 submission deadline (extensions negotiable) will be considered withdrawn and recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incremental registrations policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may add experiments to approved submissions (incremental registrations); approved Stage 2 manuscript will be accepted and authors can propose additional experiments for Stage 1 consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where experiments extend the approved submission the editorial team will seek to fast-track review. If an incremented submission is rejected, authors retain the option of publishing the most recently approved version of the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision independence from perceived novelty at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions will not be based on the perceived importance, novelty, or conclusiveness of the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While reviewers may comment on importance or novelty on the record, such comments will not influence editorial decisions at Stage 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of guidance notes and analysis scripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Raw data must be accompanied by guidance notes, where required, to assist other scientists in replicating the analysis plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to upload any relevant analysis scripts and other experimental materials that would assist in replication (e.g., stimuli & presentation code).
